gallery.title: File:North Weald Memorial - geograph.org.uk - 268896.jpg
gallery.description:
North Weald Memorial. This is the memorial to all those who served on North Weald Airfield throughout its service life especially those killed either by enemy action or accident in peacetime or in war. It stands at the old main gate to the airfield. The obelisk in the centre is the 268909 Norwegian Memorial over lost pilots designed by Roar Bjorg. North Weald opened in 1916 for home defence against Zeppelin raids. It was developed in then 1920s and '30s. It became a sector station of 11 Group. A Pilot from North Weald became the first RAF casualty of WW2 when a Hurricane Squadron from here was set upon by Spitfires from Hornchurch! North Weald was attacked many times during WW2 the memorial was erected in September 2000 on the 60th anniversary of the heaviest raid. The building in the background is Ad Astra House the old gate house
 and now 250662

gallery.title: File:North Weald ATC - geograph.org.uk - 268851.jpg
gallery.description: North Weald ATC. This is the Control Tower of North Weald Aerodrome. The goldfish bowl was a post war addition to the typical 1940’s design. North Weald had an illustrious career as a Military base from 1916 when it was known as North Weald Basset. It was developed as a Sector Station and played a key role in the Battle of Britain. It continued in use well into the “jet age” finally passing to civilian use in 1964.
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

gallery.title: File:North Weald Crash Gate - geograph.org.uk - 268810.jpg
gallery.description: North Weald Crash Gate This is Crash Gate G of North Weald aerodrome. North Weald has been active as an airfield since it was opened in 1916 to counter Zeppelin raids on London. The base was operational from 1916 until 1958 it was decommissioned as a military base in 1964. Now Boreham TL7412 is being destroyed by gravel extraction North Weald is probably the best preserved of the wartime airbases in Essex, it is home to many classic aircraft see TL4804. There is a memorial to those who served here at 268896
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland

gallery.title: File:Skymasters at North Weald - geograph.org.uk - 270635.jpg
gallery.description: Skymasters at North Weald. This is one of the hangars on 270610. Standing outside are a brace of Douglas DC4 Skymasters. When seen at a distance I thought they were Dakotas but a quick count of the engines put me right! Technically as these are in USAF livery they should carry the C54 designation. They could hold up to 54 people whereas the DC3/C47 had only 32 seats even in its post war "super" DC3 version. See also 268896
categories: Images from Geograph Britain and Ireland
